title: Rigveda 10.41: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.41: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.41 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 780v-781r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.41.1-2 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 8, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 780v
translation.original_text:
1sa̱mā̱nam u̱ tyam pu̍ruhū̱tam u̱kthya1̱̍ṁ ratha̍ṁ trica̱kraṁ sava̍nā̱ gani̍gmatam | pari̍jmānaṁ vida̱thya̍ṁ suvṛ̱ktibhi̍r va̱yaṁ vyu̍ṣṭā u̱ṣaso̍ havāmahe ||
2prā̱ta̱ryuja̍ṁ nāsa̱tyādhi̍ tiṣṭhathaḥ prāta̱ryāvā̍ṇam madhu̱vāha̍na̱ṁ ratha̍m | viśo̱ yena̱ gaccha̍tho̱ yajva̍rīr narā kī̱reś ci̍d ya̱jñaṁ hotṛ̍mantam aśvinā ||
translation.text:
1THAT general Car of yours, invoked by many a man, that comes to our libations, three-wheeled, meet for lauds, That circumambient Car, worthy of sacrifice, we call with our pure hymns at earliest flush of dawn.
2Ye, O Nâsatyas, mount that early-harnessed Car, that travels early, laden with its freight of balm, Wherewith ye, Heroes, visit clans who sacrifice, even the poor man's worship where the priest attends.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 780v (numbered 96v by the scribe) (OPenn image 781, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.40.12 ‹vājinīvasūitivājinī-vasū ni aśvinā hṛt-su›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 781r (numbered 97r by the scribe), begins in RV 10.41.3 ‹-su-hastyam agnidham vā dhṛta-dakṣam›. Verses 10.41.1-2 end on this page.

2prātaḥ-yujam | nāsatyā | adhi | tiṣṭhathaḥ | prātaḥ-yāvānam | madhu-vāhanam | ratham | viśaḥ | yena | gacchataḥ | yajvarīḥ | narā | kīreḥ | cit | yajñam | hotṛ-mantam | aśvinā

translation.original_ref: RV 10.41.3 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 8, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 781r
translation.original_text: <sup>3</sup>a̱dhva̱ryuṁ vā̱ madhu̍pāṇiṁ su̱hastya̍m a̱gnidha̍ṁ vā dhṛ̱tada̍kṣa̱ṁ damū̍nasam | vipra̍sya vā̱ yat sava̍nāni̱ gaccha̱tho 'ta̱ ā yā̍tam madhu̱peya̍m aśvinā ||
translation.text: <sup>3</sup>If to the deft Adhvaryu with the meath in hand, or to the Kindler firm in strength, the household friend, Or to the sage's poured libations ye approach, come thence, O Aṣvins, now to drink the offered meath.
